scenes.title: Forty Yellow Lemons
scenes.summary: Friday morning arrives, F2 walks steadily on her rested ankle, and F1 and M4 help squeeze forty fresh lemons for opening night.
scenes.intro: Friday morning dawns bright and clear at {SHOW}—grand opening day for the Room Nine Garden Café! In the kitchen, {F2} stands happily at her counter without pillows while {F1} and {M4} roll sleeves over bowls of yellow lemons. Listen first.
story: F1
{F2}! Look at you standing at the stove on both feet!
F2
Two days on those pillows worked miracles—not a single twinge today!
M4
Good thing too, Chef, because we brought forty fresh lemons from the market.
F2
Forty lemons means four big trays of almond lemon tart for six o'clock!
F1
How many neighbours do you think will actually come tonight, {F2}?
F2
Word travels fast on {STREET} when free music and warm bread meet!
M4
I already sliced ten lemons; {F1} is beating the eggs and sugar.
F2
Did you check the big red label on the sugar jar first, {F1}?
F1
Checked twice AND tasted a pinch! Sweet as summer!
M4
What about hot tea for twenty-four cups at once, {F2}?
F2
Two big pots of black tea, two pots of fresh courtyard mint, and hot milk.
F1
Into the oven goes tray number one—six o'clock, here we come!
scenes.outro: {F2} is back on her feet, the sugar jar is verified twice, and forty lemons are turning into golden tarts for tonight. See you next time.

scenes.title: Hook Number Nine
scenes.summary: At the front desk, M1 screws a ninth brass hook onto the wooden key board and hangs the polished Room 9 key in its permanent home.
scenes.intro: Past five o'clock Friday afternoon, {M1} stands behind the front desk with his small brass screwdriver while {F1} and {M2} watch him add something new to the wooden key board. Let's listen in first.
story: M2
For fifteen years in my hands, that board only held hooks one through eight.
M1
And look on the right edge—there were two tiny screw holes under the varnish all along.
F1
No way! Hook number nine used to hang right there thirty years ago!
M1
One turn, two turns... solid brass hook number nine, back where it belongs.
F1
May I hang the big sunroom key on it, {M1}?
M1
Go right ahead, {F1}. You earned it this week.
M2
Wait—{M1}, what is that laminated card tucked inside your paper ledger?
F1
Aha! Did you secretly keep a copy of my printed café menu, {M1}?!
M1
Only because your big numbers are easy to read without a lamp.
M2
Write this day down in the guest book: {M1} praised a printed page!
M1
Don't celebrate too much, boss. Paper books still win when it rains.
F1
Look at the courtyard clock—half past five! Let us light the lanterns!
scenes.outro: Brass hook number nine is back on the wooden board, and even {M1} keeps {F1}'s printed menu in his notebook. See you in the courtyard next time.

scenes.title: Twenty-Four Chairs After All
scenes.summary: At 5:45 PM, neighbours start streaming through the open gate early, proving M2's accidental twenty-four-chair order was exactly what they needed.
scenes.intro: At a quarter to six under warm courtyard lanterns, {F1} and {M3} are setting out teacups when {M2} rushes back from the open street gate wide-eyed. Listen first.
story: M2
{F1}! {M3}! Come look at the pavement outside our gate!
F1
It is only a quarter to six—are people arriving already?!
M2
The bookshop owner, the pharmacist, the baker's cousin, and twelve neighbours!
M3
All twelve chairs inside Room Nine just filled up in three minutes!
F1
Wait—what about those extra twelve folding chairs under the courtyard arch?!
M2
The ones I ordered by mistake on Saturday?!
M3
Unfold all twelve around the four outdoor courtyard tables right now!
F1
Every single one of your twenty-four bargain chairs has a guest, {M2}!
M2
Did you hear that, {F1}?! My mistake was actually a brilliant business plan!
F1
Take the bow, {M2}, and hand out the menu cards with a smile!
M3
Open the arched windows wide so everyone under the tree hears the piano!
M2
Welcome, friends, welcome! Hot mint tea is coming right out!
scenes.outro: Every single one of {M2}'s twenty-four bargain chairs fills with smiling neighbours under the courtyard lanterns! See you next time.

scenes.title: Sold Out in Fifteen Minutes
scenes.summary: F2, F1, and M4 race happily between kitchen and courtyard as nearly every slice of lemon tart sells out in fifteen minutes.
scenes.intro: At the bustling café counter, {F2} slices golden tarts onto white plates as fast as {F1} and {M4} can carry trays out to the tables. Listen to the whole scene first.
story: F1
Two mint teas and three lemon tarts for table four under the tree!
F2
Coming right up! {M4}, take the hot teapot to the corner window table!
M4
Table two says this almond crust is the best pastry on {STREET}!
F2
Tell table two the secret was my two kitchen apprentices on Wednesday!
F1
How many slices of lemon tart are left on tray four, {F2}?
F2
Count them: one, two, three—out of forty slices in fifteen minutes!
M4
Good thing you baked two extra trays of warm cinnamon rolls just in case!
F1
Listen—the room just went quiet! Someone is tapping a music stand!
F2
Our neighbour from number ten brought his violin case inside Room Nine!
M4
Leave the clean plates for five minutes, both of you—come listen at the door!
F2
Save those last three slices of tart for {F3}, {M1}, and {M2}!
F1
Aprons off—it is six o'clock on Friday!
scenes.outro: Thirty-seven slices of tart vanish in fifteen minutes, and the whole courtyard falls quiet as six o'clock arrives. See you inside Room 9 next time.

scenes.title: Courtyard Waltz Complete
scenes.summary: Inside the glowing glass sunroom, F3 introduces the completed thirty-year-old waltz and plays it to warm applause from the whole courtyard.
scenes.intro: Six o'clock arrives in {CITY}. Inside the warm glow of Room 9, {F3} stands beside the walnut upright piano while {M2}, {F1}, and two dozen neighbours listen through the open green shutters. Listen first.
story: F3
Good evening, friends, and welcome back to Friday tea in Room Nine.
M2
Thirty years ago in May, my aunt started a little waltz right at this piano.
F3
Rain interrupted page two—until {F1} and {M1} opened these shutters again.
F1
And tonight, our neighbour from number ten joins {F3} on the violin!
F3
Ready on three, my friend? One, two, three...
F1
Listen to the violin soar when the piano reaches middle D, {M2}!
M2
Even my glasses are misty—and for once I know right where they are!
F1
Look outside: people walking down {STREET} have stopped by the gate to listen!
F3
And there is our gentle final chord, one octave high—home again.
M2
Bravo! Bravo, {F3}! Hear the whole courtyard clapping!
F3
Take a bow yourself, {M2}—your aunt's Friday room is alive again.
F1
And nobody wants to go home yet—time for the cinnamon rolls!
scenes.outro: Piano and violin carry the finished 'Courtyard Waltz' out into the warm Friday night to heartfelt applause. See you next time.

scenes.title: A Table Every Friday
scenes.summary: Under the lanterns, M3 tells M4 and F2 he has rented a ground-floor design studio on their street so he can move back to the city and share a Friday table with M4 every week.
scenes.intro: After the applause settles into happy conversation, {M3} and {M4} sit at a small courtyard table under the tree as {F2} brings out warm cinnamon rolls. Let's listen in first.
story: F2
Two warm cinnamon rolls as my gift for my best soup-and-bread crew!
M4
Sit down for a minute, {F2}—{M3} has big news to tell us.
F2
Wait—don't tell me your Saturday morning train was cancelled, {M3}!
M3
Better: I am only taking that train to pack my boxes and move back.
M4
Tell {F2} what you signed on {STREET} this afternoon, little brother!
M3
There was an empty ground-floor studio four doors past the bakery.
F2
No way! You are opening your acoustic design studio on our street?!
M3
By day I draw quiet rooms, and after City Hall {M4} brings Grandfather's wood tools!
M4
Evenings and weekends, we are building wooden tables and panels together!
F2
Then I am reserving this exact courtyard table for you two every Friday at six!
M4
Put it in {M1}'s paper book in permanent ink, {F2}!
M3
From a swapped blue suitcase on Monday to neighbours for good!
scenes.outro: Two brothers who barely spoke two weeks ago now share a studio project right down the street—with a standing Friday table under the tree! See you next time.

scenes.title: Staying On
scenes.summary: As the last neighbours head home, F3 asks F1 and M1 if she can stay another fortnight in Room 4 and play every Friday evening.
scenes.intro: Around nine o'clock, the courtyard grows peaceful again as {F1} and {M1} stack clean white teacups inside Room 9 while {F3} closes the walnut piano lid gently. Listen first.
story: M1
Not one chipped cup, zero blown fuses, and twenty-four happy neighbours.
F1
You are smiling, {M1}! I saw it clearly under the lamp!
M1
Must be a trick of the frosted glass, {F1}.
F3
{F1}, before you close the big paper reservation book tonight...
F1
Is everything all right in Room Four, {F3}? Did the buzzer ring twice again?
F3
I have grown quite fond of that double ring—is Room Four free next week?
F1
Wait—you want to extend your stay with us, {F3}?!
F3
Two more weeks, if you will have me—and I will play every Friday for tea!
M1
Room Four belongs to you as long as you want it, madam.
F1
Written in pencil right here! {F2} and {M2} will be thrilled!
F3
Oh, by the way, the postman slipped a thick foreign postcard into the gate box.
F1
Evening mail on a Friday? Let us take it to the front desk!
scenes.outro: {F3} stays on as Room 9's Friday pianist, and a late postcard waits in the gate box! One final scene for Season 2—let's listen.

scenes.title: Under the Third Stone
scenes.summary: Closing the front desk for the night, F1, M1, and M2 read a 30th-anniversary May postcard mailed from abroad asking if the old tin capsule is still buried under the third stone from the courtyard tree.
scenes.intro: At ten o'clock Friday night, {F1}, {M1}, and {M2} gather under the warm front-desk lamp as {F1} turns over the thick stamped postcard from the gate box. Listen first.
story: M2
Look at the postmark from two weeks ago! Who writes to {SHOW} from abroad?
F1
Listen to this: 'Dear Courtyard Friends, thirty years ago this May I stayed in Room Eight!'
M1
Thirty years ago this May—that exact rainy week! Read the rest, {F1}.
F1
'I was a young mapmaker, and your sunroom tea saved my wet maps.'
M2
Room Eight! Let me check my aunt's green guest book—yes, the mapmaker is right here!
F1
Keep listening: 'Before my long journey home, your aunt and I hid a small tin time capsule.'
M2
A time capsule?! In MY courtyard?!
M1
Does the mapmaker say where they hid it, {F1}?
F1
'If you ever reopen Room Nine, count three flat stones north from the old tree!'
M2
Three flat stones north from the tree?! That is right under table number one!
M1
Hold on—when I levelled table one at dusk, that third stone sounded hollow!
F1
Grab the lantern, gentlemen—Room Nine is open, and our next mystery starts under the tree!
scenes.outro: Room 9 is open, the courtyard café is thriving, and three stones from the old shade tree sits a hollow flagstone hiding a thirty-year-old time capsule! Season 2 of {SHOW} is complete—see you in Season 3!
